text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League fixture as Brighton host Fulham at the Amex Stadium!
Brighton are looking to get back to winning ways in the Premier League after enduring a difficult run in recent weeks.

While the Seagulls managed a 2-2 draw with Liverpool on their last league outing at the Amex, that result was sandwiched between a 6-1 thrashing at Aston Villa and a 2-1 defeat at Manchester City, leaving them seventh in the table ahead of kick-off.

This is Brighton's longest winless run in the league since they failed to win any of their first five games under Roberto De Zerbi last year, but they did taste victory in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday, beating Ajax 2-0.

Fulham, meanwhile, have taken a respectable 11 points from their first nine games of the season to sit six points clear of the relegation zone, and they received a huge boost earlier this week as boss Marco Silva penned a three-year contract extension at Craven Cottage.

In the short term, Silva's main objective must be to solve Fulham's goalscoring woes – Bobby De Cordova-Reid (two goals) remains the only Fulham player to net more than once in the Premier League this season.

De Zerbi makes six changes to the team which started Thursday's European win over Ajax, with their goalscorers from that game – Joao Pedro and Fati – joining Milner, Van Hecke, Veltman and Gilmour in dropping to the bench.
Ferguson, Lallana, Baleba, Dahoud, Webster and Igor come in.
Webster may play at full-back with both Pervis Estupinan and Tariq Lamptey sidelined by injury.
Silva makes three changes to Fulham's starting lineup from Monday's 2-0 defeat at Tottenham.
Carlos Vinicius misses out with a minor injury, so Jimenez leads the line, while Reed and Iwobi replace Lukic and Pereira further back.
Silva is still without right-sided centre-backs Issa Diop and Tosin Adarabioyo, so Bassey – who struggled against Spurs – keeps his place alongside Ream.
Brighton scored a league-high 19 goals from open play across the first nine matchdays of the Premier League season, but they are without a clean sheet in 13 league outings.
There is usually plenty of goalmouth action when the Seagulls are involved, but will that be the case here? The players are making their way out of the tunnel ahead of kick-off!
Following a minute's applause to mark the recent deaths of Manchester United legend Bobby Charlton and Everton chairman Bill Kenwright, we are under way at the Amex.
Fulham are wearing a very bright pink away kit for this one, with Brighton moving the ball patiently inside their own territory in driving rain on the south coast.
It looks like Brighton are employing a back three here, at least while in possession.
Webster is playing to the right of Dunk, with Igor to the left, as they look to invite Fulham's press.
Gross – making his 200th Premier League appearance – is wide on the right with Mitoma on the left.
Fulham finally get a foot on the ball after a sustained spell of Brighton possession.
Robinson looks for Willian with a throughball into the left channel, but Webster comes across with a good sliding challenge.
Unlucky! Fulham threaten as Robinson threads a good pass into the feet of Jimenez, who had Dunk pinned.
The Mexican lays it off for Iwobi, but his touch inside the area is loose and Brighton escape.
Now Mitoma gets his first chance to advance down the Brighton left, with the Japan star reaching the byline before looking for a cutback.
It's behind Ferguson, though, and a luminous pink shirt gets to the loose ball before any of Brighton's midfield runners.
GREAT DOUBLE SAVE! How are Brighton not ahead?! A patient move ends with Baleba finding space to shoot from the edge of the box.
He looks for the top-left corner with a sweet strike, but Leno dives across to push it away.

Mitoma keeps the attack alive with a looping cross which evades Robinson and finds Adingra at the far post, but Leno pokes it to safety with his right foot before the Brighton man can finish into a gaping net!
Brighton fail to make anything of the first corner of the game.
Robinson then goes up the other end to win a corner off Webster, which Willian will take.
We've had a breathless start to this game on the south coast!
Willian's delivery is cleared to the edge of the box, where Reed's unorthodox header skips off the wet turf and goes wide.
Steele looked to have that one covered.

Brighton are looking to do something they have never done here – beat Fulham in the Premier League! The Seagulls have failed to win any of the teams' six all-time meetings in the competition (three draws, three defeats), the most they have faced any team without winning.
Webster finds Adingra with a lovely ball down the right to get Brighton on the front foot.
However, Fulham recover well to get men behind the ball and force their hosts back.
Over! Mitoma beats Castagne a total of three times with a trademark, jinking run down the wing.
His cutback finds Lallana, who in turn offloads for Baleba, but the recent arrival hammers his shot over the crossbar from the edge of the area.
Brighton are finding their groove.
Ferguson flicks it into Lallana with the outside of his boot, and the former Liverpool man lays it off for the lively Adingra to shoot over the bar from 25 yards out.
It's a disappointing finish, but the approach play was good.
Fulham have only played more Premier League games against Norwich City (eight) without ever losing than they have against Brighton (six), doing the double over the Seagulls in 2022-23.
CHANCE! Lallana pulls wide to combine with Dahoud, who releases Mitoma into the box with a terrific backheel.
Mitoma appears to get caught in two minds as he bears down on Leno with options in the middle, and his cross-shot is well wide!
Brighton have definitely upped the ante in the last 10 minutes or so, carving out two or three excellent opportunities.
But for now, Fulham remain on level terms.
The home fans aren't happy at all here.
Palhinha leaves Gross in a heap on the edge of the Fulham area with a reckless challenge.
The Fulham man is lucky not to concede a foul after appearing to lead with his arm.
There was a brief VAR check to ascertain whether Palhinha's challenge was red-card worthy, and Gross is still deep in conversation with the referee.
It was quickly cleared by the officials, but that was – at the very least – reckless from Palhinha.
Baleba does brilliantly to manoeuvre away from Palhinha as Brighton advance into the Fulham half again.
Dahoud latches onto Mitoma's pass down the left to win a corner, crossing behind off Ream.
Wide! Gross works the corner short, and Lallana is eventually found in an inside-left position.
His cross takes a wicked deflection off Robinson and goes just wide of the near post with Leno stranded.
Brighton's second corner in quick succession is less well-worked! Mitoma looks for a reverse pass which fools all of his team-mates and runs out for a goal-kick!
Brighton have had 79.9 per cent of the possession so far.
They have been utterly dominant after a bright first five minutes from Fulham, but they don't have a goal to show for their work.
GOOOOOAAAAALLL! FERGUSON WITH THE OPENER! Brighton's dominance pays off as Ferguson strokes the ball past Leno from the edge of the box.
Reed's loose pass is cut out by Igor, who advances over halfway before finding Gross.
He slips a neat pass into the feet of Ferguson, who turns and finds the bottom-left corner with a lovely side-footed finish!
Gross had options right and left as he advanced towards the Fulham area but opted to find Ferguson, who did the rest with a lovely finish!
Fulham can't have any complaints about this scoreline – they have been second-best in every department here.
Brighton threaten again as Adingra cuts inside, but Palhinha takes the ball with a great sliding challenge.
That goal was Ferguson's fifth in the Premier League this season – three of them came in an impressive win over Newcastle United on this ground a few weeks ago.
With the way this game has started, he may fancy a few more here...
We're past the half-hour mark, and we're yet to see anything of Fulham as an attacking force.
Jimenez has struggled to hold the ball up on the rare occasions where he's had a touch, with Brighton in command of possession and looking comfortable.
Robinson has been Fulham's brightest player early on.
He intercepts a lofted pass from Ferguson and the visitors can enjoy a spell on the ball, albeit inside their own territory.
That's better from the visitors as Reed breaks into the box to win a corner on the right-hand side.
Willian goes over to take it...
Wide! Webster flings himself at the set-piece delivery with a diving header, sending it as far clear as Robinson, who sends a wild shot well wide from 30 yards out – that's a real waste.
There's a brief VAR check on a potential Fulham penalty, with a question over whether the ball struck Webster on his upper arm as he stooped to head it clear.
There's absolutely no way that can be considered handball, however, and the VAR agrees – check over.
De Cordova-Reid wins a free-kick 30 yards from goal in a central position.
Willian looks for Castagne from a training-ground routine... but his pass is absolutely terrible and it runs beyond everyone for a Brighton goal-kick.
The rain is absolutely teeming down now as Willian fails to win a corner for Fulham.
We'll see how these frankly dreadful conditions affect the game as we approach the end of the first half.
Over! Iwobi dispossesses Dunk before finding Willian as Fulham break.

The Brazilian reaches the left corner of the Brighton area before trying an audacious outside-of-the-boot cross to De Cordova-Reid, who sends an awkward volley over the crossbar! Steele is still yet to be tested.
Save! Ferguson gets between two pink shirts to bring down a long pass forward.
With little support, he whips a low effort towards the near post, but Leno reads it well and is able to make a comfortable save.
Fulham are enjoying a better spell now, but their decision-making in the final third leaves much to be desired.
Willian fails to find a team-mate with a cutback from the right side of the box, then Jimenez gets another chance but crosses straight into the chest of Dunk.
We're into the final two minutes of the first half here, with Brighton back in possession.
Mitoma cuts inside before finding Ferguson, but he fouls Reed as the duo battle for the ball near the edge of the Fulham area.
Gross' positioning is an interesting one.
The German is continually drifting inside from what looks like a right wing-back role, with Adingra and Mitoma playing very high on either flank.
It's certainly a fluid Brighton system.
We're into two minutes of first-half stoppage time as the rain finally appears to be relenting.
Jimenez goes down following a coming-together with Igor, but there's no foul and the Fulham striker is quickly back to his feet.
Brighton are looking to see out the rest of the first period by controlling possession inside their own half.
HALF-TIME: BRIGHTON 1-0 FULHAM.
Brighton take a 1-0 lead into the interval against Fulham, and in truth, it's the least the Seagulls deserve for a dominant first-half performance.

Leno had already been forced into two fine saves – to keep out Baleba and Adingra – before Ferguson put the hosts ahead, turning on Gross' pass before stroking a cultured finish into the bottom-left corner.

Fulham improved at the end of the half but are yet to create a clear-cut opening, and they are perhaps fortunate to still have their full complement after Palhinha got away with a clear elbow on Gross.
While Brighton have enjoyed 72.5 per cent of the possession and hit the target with four of eight shots, Fulham have only managed three attempts in total and are yet to hit the target.
Jimenez has looked isolated up front and Willian has struggled out wide.
What can Silva do to turn the tide?
Brighton get the second half under way through Ferguson! Will it be more one-way traffic, or can Fulham find a route back into this game?
Silva decided against making any half-time substitutions.
With Adama Traore and Carlos Vinicius out, he has his hands tied in attack somewhat.
Bassey looks for Jimenez with a long ball over the top, but it's an easy one for Steele to claim.
Fulham are definitely pressing Brighton with more intensity in the early stages of this second half, but De Zerbi's team are adept at playing through the pressure.
Lallana beats Ream with an excellent turn on the edge of Fulham's area and is chopped down, giving the hosts a free-kick in a great position.
OFF THE BAR! Brighton captain Dunk claims the set-piece for himself, whipping a lovely effort up and over the wall.
Leno is beaten, but the ball bounces off the top of the crossbar and goes over.
So unlucky!
Brighton scored and conceded in their first nine Premier League games of the season.
Though the Seagulls will want a clean sheet here, they could yet become the first top-flight side to see goals at both ends in their first 10 matches of a campaign since Tottenham in 1988-89.
Dahoud scampers over halfway and appears to be brought down by Bassey 25 yards from goal, but the referee waves play on.
Fulham get enough men behind the ball to force Brighton to recycle possession.
Ahead of this weekend's fixtures, Fulham ranked 18th in the Premier League for total shots (96) and shots on target (30) this season.
Only Sheffield United (two) and Luton Town (three) have scored fewer goals from open play than their five this term.
They have really lacked attacking inspiration again here.
Fulham finally manage a shot on target, but it's an easy one for Steele to deal with as Willian sends a tame effort straight at the Brighton shot-stopper from 25 yards out.
Fulham waste another promising position as Iwobi turns Baleba to reach the byline before overrunning it and conceding a goal-kick.
Silva has seen enough, with Pereira and Muniz preparing to enter the fray.
Brighton win a free-kick 35 yards from goal as Palhinha clatters into Lallana.
The Fulham midfielder has an exasperated look on his face, but that was definitely a foul.
Robinson gets up to head Gross' delivery away, then Willian is back to deal with Dunk's second ball into the area.
Brighton recycle possession patiently before winning a throw-in, which will allow Fulham to make their changes...
Pereira takes Reed's place in midfield.
Jimenez is withdrawn after yet another Premier League outing without a goal.
Muniz replaces the frustrated Mexican.
Fulham make a third switch as De Cordova-Reid trudges off, to be replaced by Wilson.
De Zerbi responds with one change of his own as Fati takes Lallana's place.
Over! Fulham are penned back again as Mitoma advances down the left before offloading for Baleba.
He shoots from the edge of the box... but it's always rising and Leno is untroubled between the sticks.
Wilson is down in a heap just inside Brighton's half, claiming he was caught by Mitoma.
The referee didn't see it, but Mitoma caught him in the face with a loose arm, albeit accidentally.
Wilson is jeered by the home fans as he touches the ball for the first time since that coming-together.
Fulham are enjoying a better spell now, engaging Brighton much higher up the field.
Steele makes another routine save as Iwobi hits a tame effort straight at him from 25 yards.
Fulham's approach play was positive, however, with Muniz winning possession high up the pitch.
Now Pereira is claiming he was caught by a high boot from Adingra, but once again, the referee is uninterested.
GOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLL! PALHINHA LEVELS! Wow.
Fulham are level out of nowhere! Brighton lose the ball while playing out from the back, with Iwobi pressing high before feeding Wilson, who in turn picks out Palhinha.
The midfielder – who should probably have been sent off in the first half – finds the top-right corner with a brilliant strike from the edge of the D.
Substitute Wilson gets the assist, finding Palhinha with a good pass around the corner following some good pressing from the visitors.
Brighton were utterly dominant in the first half, but their standards have definitely slipped since the restart.
Fulham have been much more competitive and now they're back on terms!
ALMOST 2-1 TO FULHAM! Robinson escapes his man down the Fulham left before cutting back for Muniz.
The ball is slightly behind the substitute, who improvises with a lovely backheel, forcing Steele into a brilliant reflex save! Brighton are rocking now...
Block! Gross dances through multiple challenges to reach the Fulham area before seeing his low effort blocked at close quarters.
This game could go either way now, it's wide open!
Close! Robinson gets down the Fulham left before hitting a low shot, which goes narrowly wide of the near post.
De Zerbi can't be pleased with what he's seen in the last few minutes, and further Brighton changes are imminent.
Brighton make a triple change.
Buonanotte is on for Baleba.
Veltman takes the place of Adingra.
Gilmour replaces Dahoud in Brighton's fourth substitution of the match.
Robinson receives the first booking of the game for a late challenge on Buonanotte on halfway.
The Brighton substitute was about to break into Fulham territory but was cynically chopped down.
Palhinha is forced to go off for treatment after a collision with Fati.
There seems to be blood on the shirt of the Fulham goalscorer, and Silva is complaining to the fourth official, claiming his midfielder was elbowed.
There's another concern for Fulham as Leno goes down holding his hamstring.
The medical staff are on to tend to the shot-stopper.
Leno is going to carry on for now as the game restarts with Brighton in possession.
The home fans aren't happy with the Fulham goalkeeper, claiming he was timewasting.
Brighton have become the first top-flight team to both score and concede in their first 10 games of a league campaign since 1988-89, when Tottenham did so.
Will we get a winner as we enter the final stages?
Fulham striker Muniz is booked for a careless shove on Gross in midfield.
Brighton make another change as they look to get back on top.
Joao Pedro replaces the opening goalscorer Ferguson.
Substitutes have scored 15 Premier League goals for Brighton in 2023, only two fewer than they had scored for the Seagulls between 2017 and 2022 (17).
It's the joint most goals scored by subs in a single year by a team in Premier League history, with Spurs in 2008 and Arsenal in 2009 also seeing subs score 15 times.
We're into the final 10 minutes of the 90 here, and in truth, Fulham have carried more threat than their hosts in the last 20 minutes or so.
The awful conditions have impacted the pace of this game, with Brighton's attackers beginning to get bogged down.
Brighton win a corner on their left-hand side, which is taken quickly to Mitoma as the hosts change their angle of attack.
He cuts inside before crossing, but Bassey rises highest to clear for Fulham.
SAVE! Joao Pedro breaks in behind the Fulham backline, slightly to the left of goal.
He shoots on the turn from a tight angle, but Leno is there to keep out his weak attempt and Fulham survive.
It's all happening here! Fati goes up for a spectacular overhead kick just inside the area, and Castagne appears to nudge him slightly.
The home fans appeal for a penalty, but the referee says no and it's Castagne who stays down as Mitoma dribbles towards goal, with Bassey having to make a strong challenge to keep him out.
Castagne receives treatment as both players take the opportunity to catch their breath.
Fulham are about to make another change, but the former Leicester City full-back looks okay to continue.
Willian is the man to make way as Cairney enters the action.
We'll probably get a lengthy period of stoppage time, with Castagne being down for a full two minutes there.
He's on his feet and moving comfortably as Brighton look to build another attack.
Castagne is forced into action as Fati dribbles at him, with the Fulham man poking the ball behind for a corner to the hosts...
OFF THE LINE! Gross delivers a deep corner to the far post, where the unmarked Webster loops a header up and over Leno.
It looks destined to find the net, but Robinson gets back on the line to nod it away! So close!
We will have NINE minutes of stoppage time here! Can either team find a winning goal?
Wilson is cautioned for clear tactical foul to stop Gilmour on halfway.
The Wales international pleads his innocence, but he has no case.
Silva makes another change, and Fulham look happy to hold what they have.
Iwobi takes his time to depart as Lukic replaces him.
CHANCE! Wilson skips past Igor with ease before cutting back for Pereira.
The Brazilian sees his first shot blocked at close quarters, so he swivels to hit it on the volley at the second time of asking... but Steele gets behind it.
Veltman wins a free-kick high on the Brighton right as the hosts continue to chase a winner.
It's delivered deep, but the outstanding Robinson snuffs out the danger for Fulham.
Fulham are frustrated as Dunk goes down under pressure from Cairney.
The visitors thought they had a chance to break, but the referee grants Brighton a free-kick on halfway.
CHANCE! It's panic stations for Fulham as Brighton work it into the box.
Igor squares the ball for Buonanotte, who attempts to hold it up for a team-mate, but the massed pink shirts manage to scramble it clear.
Mitoma is dispossessed by Wilson, but the Japan winger quickly gets back to his feet to recover the ball and set Brighton away on another attack...
MISS! Mitoma crosses for Joao Pedro, who sees a shot blocked on the turn.
Buonanotte follows it up on the edge of the area... but he blazes his shot over the bar! That will surely be that, and Fulham have done enough to claim a point!
FULL-TIME: BRIGHTON 1-1 FULHAM.

The full-time whistle is blown at the Amex, and Brighton are still yet to beat Fulham in a Premier League fixture! Silva's men fight back to take a point from an entertaining affair played out in awful weather conditions, but the hosts may have every right to feel aggrieved by the identity of the Fulham goalscorer! Brighton were dominant in the first half and went ahead when Ferguson beat Leno from the edge of the box, and Fulham could have been reduced to 10 men when Palhinha appeared to elbow Gross.
Fulham improved in the second half and that man Palhinha levelled the scores, sweeping home from the edge of the box following a high turnover.
After a frustrating second period, Brighton see their winless run stretch to four Premier League matches ahead of next week's trip to Everton.
Fulham, meanwhile, take on Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup this week before hosting Manchester United next Saturday.
Until then, it's goodbye from us, and we'll see you next time!
